prompt: Find $\begin{pmatrix}1\\2\\3\end{pmatrix}\times\begin{pmatrix}4\\5\\6\end{pmatrix}$ and verify that it is perpendicular to $\begin{pmatrix}1\\2\\3\end{pmatrix}$.
Which statement is **false** for all non-zero vectors $\mathbf v$ and $\mathbf w$?
markscheme: **B.** The vector product is anti-commutative: $\mathbf w\times\mathbf v=-(\mathbf v\times\mathbf w)$, so they are equal only when the product is $\mathbf 0$ (parallel vectors) — not for all vectors. A, C and D are true: $\mathbf v\times\mathbf v=\mathbf 0$, the product is perpendicular to both, and it is zero exactly when the vectors are parallel.

prompt: Find the area of the triangle with vertices $A(1,0,0)$, $B(0,2,0)$ and $C(0,0,3)$.
markscheme:
$\overrightarrow{AB}=\begin{pmatrix}-1\\2\\0\end{pmatrix}$, $\overrightarrow{AC}=\begin{pmatrix}-1\\0\\3\end{pmatrix}$, $\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AC}=\begin{pmatrix}6\\3\\2\end{pmatrix}$ **(M1)(A1)**

Area $=\tfrac12\sqrt{36+9+4}=\tfrac72$ **(A1)**

$|\mathbf v\times\mathbf w|$ is the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\mathbf v$ and $\mathbf w$; the triangle is half of it.
